📖Read the text اقرأ النص

صفحة 25 من الكتاب — زراعة الشاى وقطفه فى الصين القديمة

Read

00:00 / 00:00 اسحب على الشريط للتنقّل · اضغط أى كلمة فى النص للانتقال إليها

Part 1 — A medical drink for the rich The history of tea is complex and fascinating. Its history involves many different cultures and began thousands of years ago. The earliest written mention of tea was found in 3 A.D. in a book written by Hua Tuo, which describes tea as a medical drink in China. In the beginning, the only people who drank tea were the rich. Tea plants were rare, only rich people could find and buy tea leaves. For hundreds of years, Chinese people continued to drink tea for its medical qualities and religious men continued to use tea in religious ceremonies. As tea grew more popular, people began to drink tea for its taste as well as its medical benefits.

Read

00:00 / 00:00 اسحب على الشريط للتنقّل · اضغط أى كلمة فى النص للانتقال إليها

Part 2 — Tea reaches the world The Chinese government started planting tea and building tea shops in 618 A.D. This allowed all people to be able to enjoy tea. It also increased its availability. During the same period of time, tea also began to spread to the Japanese. Japanese students who studied in China were introduced to tea during the religious ceremonies. The Emperor of Japan enjoyed the tea and began to plant tea seeds in Japan. During the 16th century, Portuguese merchants discovered the delights of drinking tea while visiting China. In the 17th century drinking tea became popular in Britain. The British soon began importing tea through the East India Company. Tea began in Britain as a drink for the wealthy only. The British introduced tea drinking and production to India, who then had a share in China’s market. It spread throughout the population, and onwards to other countries. Today, tea is a vital part of many cultures. This drink that was once rare is enjoyed in almost every country around the world.

❓Answer the following questions أجب عن الأسئلة الآتية

صفحة 26 من الكتاب — أوراق الشاى داخل الإبريق
1- Who was the first man to mention tea in books?
اعرض الإجابة
Hua Tuo — he wrote about tea in a book in 3 A.D.
2- Tea was first known in China for its benefits. Explain.
اعرض الإجابة
It was described as a medical drink; people drank it for its medical qualities and religious men used it in religious ceremonies.
3- How did the Chinese government help in the development of tea production?
اعرض الإجابة
In 618 A.D. it started planting tea and building tea shops, which allowed all people to enjoy tea and increased its availability.
4- How was tea introduced in India?
اعرض الإجابة
The British introduced tea drinking and production to India, which then had a share in China’s market.
5- How did the Japanese know about tea?
اعرض الإجابة
Japanese students who studied in China were introduced to tea during religious ceremonies; then the Emperor of Japan enjoyed it and began planting tea seeds in Japan.
6- Why was tea a drink for the wealthy only?
اعرض الإجابة
Because tea plants were rare, so only rich people could find and buy tea leaves.

⚖️Write (True) or (False) صح أم خطأ مع التصحيح

صفحة 27 من الكتاب — صبّ الشاى فى الفنجان

Correct the false statements.

1- The Portuguese were the first people to drink tea.
اعرض الإجابة
False — The Chinese were the first; Portuguese merchants only discovered tea in the 16th century while visiting China.
2- Tea was the most available drink all over China.
اعرض الإجابة
False — At the beginning tea plants were rare and only the rich could buy them; it became available after 618 A.D.
3- Japanese merchants started selling tea in India in the 17th century.
اعرض الإجابة
False — It was the British who introduced tea to India, through the East India Company.
4- The Emperor of Japan started planting tea in Japan in the 16th century.
اعرض الإجابة
False — He planted tea seeds around 618 A.D. — the 7th century, not the 16th.
5- Tea was first known for its medical benefits.
اعرض الإجابة
True

📝Complete the paragraph أكمل الفقرة الآتية

Use words from the text to complete the paragraph below.

Tea was first discovered in ……………… . It was a ……………… drink that not every person in the Chinese ……………… could afford. Only ……………… people could find and buy tea leaves. After ……………… of years, tea started to spread in other countries like; ……………… , ……………… and ……………… .

اعرض الإجابة
Tea was first discovered in China . It was a rare drink that not every person in the Chinese population could afford. Only wealthy people could find and buy tea leaves. After hundreds of years, tea started to spread in other countries like; Japan , Portugal and Britain .

❓Think and discuss فكّر وناقش

صفحة 28 من الكتاب — الشاى الأخضر بنكهات جديدة
1- The article mentioned "medical benefits" of tea. Search for more details about the topic and share it with your class.
اعرض الإجابة
Tea is rich in antioxidants; green tea may help the heart and lower cholesterol, and it contains a small amount of caffeine that improves concentration. Camomile tea helps people relax and sleep. Too much tea, however, reduces the absorption of iron, so it should not be drunk straight after meals.
2- Nowadays, the trend is the production of tea with different flavours. What do you think of that?
اعرض الإجابة
I think flavoured tea is a clever idea: it attracts young people who do not like plain tea and it adds the benefits of fruits and herbs. On the other hand, some flavoured teas contain a lot of sugar and artificial colours, so the natural taste and benefits of tea can be lost.
